subject: Pacific sailfish held up by an angler aboard a small fishing boat, sail fully raised (Ixtapa, Mexico)
alt: Angler holding a Pacific sailfish with its tall blue-black sail raised aboard a fishing boat
author: Cruetresin
notes: Eastern Pacific sailfish photographed off Ixtapa, Mexico. Species clear: full sail plus bill. Young angler's face is visible. No jumping or tail-walking sailfish photo with an allowed license was found. Resized to WebP.

subject: Lit-up sailfish at boatside as a mate grabs the bill for release, Costa Rica
alt: Mate grabbing the bill of a lit-up sailfish beside a fishing boat in Costa Rica before release
author: Rofern223
notes: Shot in Costa Rica. The Commons description reads 'un pesce vela pescato in Costa Rica'. The sail is mostly folded, so the ID rests on the bronze lit-up bars, the bill and the source description. Mate is seen from behind. Also works as a catch-and-release image.

subject: Lit-up blue marlin alongside a sportfishing boat with a lure in its mouth, central Pacific
alt: Lit-up Pacific blue marlin alongside a sportfishing boat, electric-blue bars glowing in the water
author: quokka2
notes: Pacific blue marlin (central Pacific; sometimes split as Makaira mazara). Source is only 1903px wide, below the 2000px hero target. A deckhand's gloved hand, leg and the leader are visible at the bottom edge. This was the best live blue marlin under an allowed license.

subject: Atlantic blue marlin leaping out of the water
alt: Blue marlin leaping from the sea with its bill pointed skyward and water streaming off its body
author: NOAA
notes: Classic NOAA jump shot. The original is an upscaled older scan with visible softness and JPEG artefacts, so the large file is capped at 1400px wide. Use at small or medium size only. Muted, cool tones.

subject: Black marlin held boatside by a deckhand, South Pacific off Queensland
alt: Black marlin with rigid outstretched pectoral fins held boatside by a deckhand in the open ocean
author: jamesh111
notes: Off Queensland, Australia. The rigid, non-folding pectoral fins confirm black marlin. Portrait orientation. The deckhand's arm and torso are partly visible.

subject: Lit-up striped marlin swimming boatside on the leader off Carrillo, Guanacaste, Costa Rica
alt: Lit-up striped marlin with violet-blue fins and stripes swimming boatside off Carrillo, Costa Rica
author: Jackiemora01
notes: Shot in Costa Rica (Playa Carrillo, Guanacaste). Sharp and vivid. The leader line is visible, consistent with a release.

subject: Large yellowfin tuna swimming in deep blue water
alt: Large yellowfin tuna swimming in deep blue water showing yellow finlets and long sickle-shaped fins
author: Almcglashan (Al McGlashan)
notes: Underwater shot of a big yellowfin with more tuna in the background. Sharp, saturated blue.

subject: School of yellowfin tuna underwater
alt: School of yellowfin tuna with bright yellow finlets swimming together underwater
author: Marc Taquet / IFREMER
notes: IFREMER research photo. Probably taken around a FAD or net enclosure, and some netting may show near the bottom edge.

subject: Hooked dorado (mahi-mahi) leaping out of deep blue water, Costa Rica
alt: Golden-green dorado (mahi-mahi) leaping from deep blue Pacific water while hooked off Costa Rica
author: Galo Malavasi (Galomalavasi)
notes: Sportfishing in Costa Rica (title 'Mahi Mahi Costa Rica'). Cropped to remove the photographer's logo mark at top right, so the result is portrait. The fishing line is visible.

subject: Angler on a boat holding a large female dorado (mahi-mahi)
alt: Angler aboard a boat holding a large female dorado (mahi-mahi) with gold-green coloring
author: Distad
notes: Female (cow) dorado caught off Jamaica, 54 in / 34 lb. Slightly hazy, overcast light. Angler's face is visible.

subject: Angler holding a roosterfish showing its comb-like dorsal fin
alt: Angler holding a roosterfish showing its long comb-like dorsal fin spines on a sunny ocean day
author: Carol Neuhoff
notes: The comb dorsal fin and dark curved bands confirm Nematistius pectoralis. Teen angler's face is visible, and his T-shirt has club text. Source is 1971px wide.

subject: Roosterfish lying on beach sand, comb dorsal fin raised (Mexico)
alt: Roosterfish lying on beach sand showing its striking comb dorsal fin and silver-blue body
author: Fredy (via iNaturalist)
notes: Clean ID shot of a shore-caught fish on sand, Pacific Mexico. Not gory. Wide, narrow source (2048x923).

subject: Wahoo swimming in open blue water
alt: Wahoo swimming in clear blue water showing its long torpedo body and vertical tiger stripes
author: Michael Bommerer
notes: Live underwater photo. Sharp and correctly identified: long snout and blue-grey vertical bars.

subject: Large cubera snapper on a Caribbean reef
alt: Large grey cubera snapper with faint bars swimming over a coral reef
author: Henrya (via iNaturalist)
notes: Atlantic or Caribbean reef photo. In Pacific Costa Rica the 'cubera' is usually L. novemfasciatus (Pacific dog snapper/cubera), so caption generically. Muted blue-green underwater cast. 2048px wide.

subject: Pacific red snapper (pargo rojo / huachinango), studio specimen photo
alt: Pacific red snapper (pargo rojo) with bright red fins and pink-silver body on a white background
author: Warren E. Savary / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
notes: Species is Lutjanus peru, the Pacific red snapper caught in Costa Rica. FDA reference image cropped to remove the colour card, scale bar and labels. Clean studio shot on white, not a live photo.

subject: School of tarpon swimming over a reef
alt: School of silver tarpon swimming above a reef in sunlit blue water
author: Albert Kok
notes: Live underwater shot, Caribbean. No tarpon jumping photo with an allowed license was found.

subject: Close view of a tarpon showing large silver scales
alt: Silver tarpon with large mirror-like scales and upturned mouth swimming underwater
author: Daiju Azuma
notes: Aquarium photograph, but sharp and clean.

subject: Common snook specimen showing its black lateral line
alt: Common snook with its distinctive black lateral line stripe and yellow fins
author: jose_colorado-dapa (via iNaturalist)
notes: Freshly caught common snook (Mexico) on a light surface, with a small red mark near the pectoral fin. Caribbean-side species. Pacific Costa Rica has the closely related black snook (C. nigrescens/viridis). Source is 2048px wide.

subject: Greater amberjack cruising over a rocky reef
alt: Greater amberjack cruising over a rocky reef in deep blue water with baitfish behind
author: NOAA Photo Library (National Marine Sanctuaries)
notes: Live underwater shot. Sharp. The dark nuchal band through the eye confirms Seriola dumerili.

subject: Goliath grouper resting on a sandy seabed
alt: Goliath grouper resting on a sandy seabed, its mottled olive-brown body facing the camera
author: Dan Schofield (via iNaturalist)
notes: Atlantic goliath grouper (Florida/Caribbean). The Pacific counterpart in Costa Rica is E. quinquefasciatus. Caption as 'grouper' generically if needed. 2048px wide.

subject: Guapote / rainbow bass (wolf cichlid)
alt: Guapote (rainbow bass) with a black-speckled body, a prized freshwater game fish of Costa Rica
author: Sesamehoneytart
notes: Aquarium photo of a large adult. The ID is correct: P. dovii's dense black speckling and big jaw. This is the Lake Arenal 'guapote'.

subject: Pacific sierra mackerel, freshly caught (Ecuador)
alt: Pacific sierra mackerel with rows of golden-orange spots on a silver body
author: juanrrx (via iNaturalist)
notes: The exact species, Pacific sierra, which is common off Costa Rica. Specimen photo on a light surface. 2048px wide.

subject: Skipjack tuna on a wooden deck
alt: Skipjack tuna with dark horizontal belly stripes lying on a dark wooden boat deck
author: Karg se
notes: Accurate skipjack tuna (belly stripes). Dead fish on deck, no gore. Faint red at the tail base.

subject: Black skipjack (barrilete negro) swimming, Baja California Sur
alt: Black skipjack tuna (barrilete negro) swimming in blue water with dark stripes along its back
author: Diego Delso
notes: This is black skipjack (Euthynnus lineatus), NOT Katsuwonus. It is the 'skipjack' Pacific Costa Rica anglers most often catch. Label it 'black skipjack'. Excellent underwater photo.

subject: Angler in Costa Rica holding a Pacific crevalle jack caught on a lure
alt: Angler on a boat in Costa Rica holding a big Pacific crevalle jack caught on a lure
author: David Mailland
notes: Shot in Costa Rica, 2014. Caranx caninus, the Pacific crevalle jack, sometimes treated as C. hippos. Small hook wound visible. Angler's face visible.

subject: Swordfish swimming near the surface in open ocean
alt: Swordfish swimming near the surface in bright blue open ocean water
author: sylvain_eichhorn (via iNaturalist)
notes: Optional slot. A rare live swordfish photo, but the source is only 1449px wide (below the 1600px target) and the image is soft. Use small.

subject: Underwater sardine school / bait ball (Moalboal, Philippines)
alt: Dense school of silver sardines swirling underwater in a shimmering bait ball
author: Lakshmi Sawitri
notes: Moalboal sardine run, Philippines. Generic baitfish school.
